A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation-learning study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical descriptions, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original VQA experiments on three synthetic datasets and VQA-v2, together with property-prediction and supplementary analyses. Results appear throughout Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical study and adds GQA experiments, including accuracy, computational-cost, model-size, and question-category results.

M1.justification: The representation models, frozen T5 encoder, representation conversions, transformer classifier, and training objectives remain unchanged. GQA reuses the real-world model adaptations already described for VQA-v2; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v4 adds balanced GQA while retaining all four earlier datasets. Its five question categories and 1,834 answers substantially broaden real-world reasoning coverage beyond v3's VQA-v2 subset restricted to yes/no and numerical answers (Section 3.3; Appendix B; Table 6).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments. The new GQA evaluation reuses the six foundation models, ResNet SA, STEVE, DINOSAURv2, and question-only baseline already evaluated on VQA-v2; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: The added GQA experiment introduces balanced train/testdev evaluation, its own splits, and downstream training for 900k steps with batch size 32 and learning rate 0.0001 (Appendices A.3 and B; Table 6). Existing synthetic and VQA-v2 protocols and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v4 extends the downstream-capacity and computational-cost analyses to GQA and adds GQA question-category difficulty and rank-correlation analyses (Figures 4, 14, 17, and 28). These extend existing analytical questions; the property-prediction, upstream-metric, training-size, and VAE investigations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds and 95% confidence intervals where available, with one seed for foundation models, and retain the same STEVE seed-selection disclosure. GQA follows these practices. Some plotted interval values change, but no revised statistical procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: v4 adds a substantial GQA result suite, including T-15 accuracies of 51.3% for DINOv2 and 51.1% for DINOSAURv2 (Table 14), plus scaling and category findings. Figures 3 and 14 also revise DINOSAURv2's T-15 curves: approximately 94.3% to 95.8% on CLEVR and 94.4% to 93.8% on Multi-dSprites. Tables 7–13 remain unchanged, leaving unexplained plot/table discrepancies.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of representation reshaping, projection, classification, and property-prediction matching are retained. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs, or new formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The stated empirical contribution expands from 640 downstream models on three synthetic and one real-world dataset to 684 models on three synthetic and two real-world datasets. The central claims about foundation-model competitiveness, object-centric computational advantages, and weak global VAE representations remain.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies cross-category consistency with the GQA exception and proposes greater reliance on linguistic cues as an explanation for Logical and Compare questions (Section 4.2). Section 3.6 removes v3's discussion of independent synthetic object properties and its explicit disclaimer about optimizing VQA performance, while retaining the unequal-pretraining caveat.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B document GQA training schedules, splits, seven slots, preprocessing, and reuse of VQA-v2 architecture settings. Acknowledgments add JUPITER/JUWELS computing resources, while the A100 footnote drops the 40GB memory specification. Most existing implementation and reproducibility information is retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hudson and Manning's GQA reference, Liu et al. (2022) for the linguistic-cue interpretation, and a Jülich computing-resource reference. The related-work argument and positioning remain substantially unchanged; most other reference edits concern style or bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract, limitations, real-world discussion, and conclusion receive localized rewrites, with added GQA explanations and expanded acknowledgments. Citations switch to author-year format, but the main section sequence and Appendix A–D organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 4 expands into three panels; Figures 9, 14, and 17 gain GQA panels; Figure 28 and Table 14 are added; and Table 6 gains a GQA row. The ICLR template changes title styling, headers, and placement, while most existing graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: GQA strengthens the study by testing broader real-world reasoning than v3's restricted VQA-v2 subset, and its capacity and category analyses expose a useful exception to cross-question consistency. This provides a limited net improvement. The benefit is tempered by unreconciled DINOSAURv2 discrepancies between revised Figures 3/14 and retained Tables 7/12, and by the still broadly worded cross-category takeaway.
